correctness.rationale: At a minimum of m squares, an empty row and empty column are impossible. Occupancy and the outside-neighbor formula r_i+c_j restrict every positive column count to 1 or m. This gives all families in both aspect-ratio cases. The intersection bound proves the isolates. A dependency path/cycle argument establishes the exact injection distance t+c and the sharp diameter. Two standalone standard-library programs agree with the symbolic statements on specified finite ranges.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The final result asserts a significantly stronger configuration-space theorem. Numerical equality gamma_12=gamma supplies no count or mobility, and the 2013 two-row observation cannot be extrapolated to m>=3 without the column-count restriction and arrangement-graph analysis proved here. We do not claim originality for the abstract arrangement graph or its diameter: novelty would be defeated if an older source already established the relevant minimum-set classification or the entire reconfiguration graph.

originality.rationale: The numerical minimum and the two-row [1,2]-set case are prior results. Day–Tripathi (1992) already introduced arrangement graphs with their standard degree and diameter, so those graph invariants are also not separately new. The claim is the full optimum-set classification for m,n>=3 and its identification with a known arrangement graph plus isolated configurations, with a sharp square-board immobility boundary. Actual published-finding corpus and literature comparisons found no stronger covering claim; unindexed work remains a priority risk.
